title: A Coordinate Protocol for Low-Bandwidth Atmospheric and Thermodynamic Sensing
subtitle: Encoding Physical State as Count Positions on a Signed Geometric Field: The Atmospheric Layer, Thermal Closures, and Binary Position Metrics
abstract_introductory_note: This paper establishes the detailed atmospheric and thermodynamic layer within the Measurement Coordinate System (MCS). Continuing the procedural record of a single physical unit counting itself inward via halving under the sqrt(2) master mechanic, it replaces continuous statistical thermodynamics with a pure discrete count reading on a 512-vector base and presents mechanics, master tables, and binary bit-packet architectures for low-bandwidth atmospheric telemetry.

axiom_and_binary_split.axiom: There is exactly one physical unit.
axiom_and_binary_split.count_0: The uncut floor, the absolute whole prior to any operational partition.
axiom_and_binary_split.count_1: The dual base, the binary split establishing the metric of bits across negative and positive fields from the center.

count_direction_and_thermodynamic_shift.claim: sqrt(2) is the inverse thermodynamic metric.

outward_direction.meaning: Mechanical Domain Quantity; counts whole units outward.

inward_direction.meaning: The metric of inward halving read from the inside.

count_direction_and_thermodynamic_shift.depth_definition: Depth d advances once per halving and is the honest exponent.
count_direction_and_thermodynamic_shift.count_definition: Count c is the operation index and advances only when depth completes a rational-irrational pair.

local_atmospheric_temperature_differenti.description: Localized temperature variations are mapped as discrete fractional node displacements inside the Count-5 thermal envelope.

bit_shift_mechanics.heating: drives the state outward toward rational perimeter boundaries, increasing tracking sub-node bits
bit_shift_mechanics.cooling: collapses inward toward the baseline coordinate anchor, decreasing tracking bits
bit_shift_mechanics.hardware_implication: heat change is recognized as a directional address step across the geometric matrix without subtraction routines

atmospheric_telemetry.description: Atmospheric points are encoded as binary position strings rather than high-precision floats.
atmospheric_telemetry.progressive_truncation: For low-bandwidth channels, hardware can drop deep bits and the packet degrades gracefully while preserving coarser state identity.
